title: Water Quality Management
description: Standard operating procedure for water quality testing, equipment calibration, parameter maintenance, and emergency response protocols for coral nursery and holding systems. Stable water quality is fundamental to coral health - even brief parameter excursions can trigger stress responses. This SOP ensures consistent monitoring and rapid response to water quality issues.

steps.title: Water Quality Fundamentals
steps.description: Corals require stable water conditions within narrow parameter ranges. Key parameters include: temperature (24-28C for most species), salinity (33-36 ppt), pH (8.0-8.4), alkalinity (7-12 dKH), calcium (380-450 ppm), magnesium (1250-1400 ppm), and ammonia/nitrite/nitrate (0/0/<20 ppm). Consistency is more important than hitting exact targets - avoid rapid fluctuations.

steps.title: Testing Equipment Inventory
steps.description: Maintain the following water quality testing equipment in good working order:

steps.title: Daily Testing Protocol
steps.description: Conduct daily tests for temperature and salinity at minimum. Test at consistent times each day, ideally first thing in the morning before any system maintenance. Record readings immediately in the water quality log. Visual inspection of water clarity should accompany daily testing - cloudy water may indicate bacterial bloom or equipment failure. Alert supervisor if any parameter exceeds threshold.

steps.title: Weekly Testing Protocol
steps.description: In addition to daily parameters, test pH, alkalinity, and calcium weekly. Test nitrate and phosphate weekly or bi-weekly depending on system bioload. Record all results in the water quality log with date, time, and tester initials. Compare results to historical trends - sudden changes warrant investigation even if values remain within acceptable range.

steps.title: Testing Procedure Checklist
steps.description: Follow these steps for accurate water testing:
checklistItems: Rinse sample containers with tank water before collecting
Collect sample from mid-water column (not surface or bottom)
Allow sample to equilibrate to room temperature if testing offsite
Rinse probe or testing equipment between different systems
Follow manufacturer instructions for reagent volumes
Read colorimetric tests under consistent lighting
Record results immediately - do not rely on memory
Compare results to previous readings for trend analysis

steps.title: Equipment Calibration Schedule
steps.description: Calibrate pH meters before each use or minimum weekly using fresh buffer solutions. Verify refractometer accuracy with calibration fluid monthly. Replace reagents according to manufacturer expiration dates or every 6 months, whichever is sooner. Document all calibration activities in the equipment log. If readings seem inconsistent, recalibrate before assuming system problem.

steps.title: pH Meter Calibration Procedure
steps.description: Follow these steps to calibrate pH meters:
checklistItems: Gather fresh calibration buffers (pH 7.0 and 10.0 minimum)
Place probe in pH 7.0 buffer and wait for stable reading
Adjust meter to read 7.00 using calibration function
Place probe in pH 10.0 buffer and wait for stable reading
Rinse and store probe in storage solution
Record calibration date, values, and slope in log

steps.title: Parameter Excursion Response
steps.description: When parameters exceed acceptable ranges, respond immediately but carefully. NEVER make rapid corrections - changing parameters too quickly causes additional stress. Temperature: adjust by maximum 1C per hour. Salinity: adjust by maximum 1 ppt per hour. pH: investigate cause before attempting correction. Always identify the root cause of parameter drift to prevent recurrence.

steps.title: Temperature Management
steps.description: Monitor heater and chiller function daily. Temperature should remain within 1C of setpoint. For temperature emergencies: if too warm, increase airflow, add ice packs to sump (not directly to coral tank), shade from direct sunlight. If too cold, check heater function, add additional heater if needed. Never add hot water directly. Document all temperature interventions and their effectiveness.

steps.title: Salinity Management
steps.description: Salinity changes from evaporation (increases) or freshwater input (decreases). Top off evaporated water with freshwater only - never saltwater. Use auto-top-off systems with float switches for consistency. If salinity is low: allow evaporation or add small amounts of salt mix gradually. If salinity is high: add freshwater slowly over several hours. Check specific gravity/refractometer calibration if readings seem inconsistent.

steps.title: pH and Alkalinity Management
steps.description: pH and alkalinity are interconnected - alkalinity acts as a buffer maintaining stable pH. If pH is low: increase alkalinity gradually using sodium bicarbonate or commercial buffer. If pH is high: increase ventilation, check CO2 levels, reduce dosing. Alkalinity drops indicate coral calcification is occurring (positive sign) - maintain through regular dosing. Use two-part calcium/alkalinity supplements or kalkwasser for balanced supplementation.

steps.title: Nutrient Management
steps.description: Elevated nutrients (nitrate, phosphate) promote algae growth and can inhibit coral calcification. If nitrate exceeds 20 ppm: increase water changes, review feeding practices, check filtration efficiency. If phosphate exceeds 0.05 ppm: use phosphate-absorbing media, reduce feeding, increase protein skimming. Some nutrient presence is beneficial - ultra-low nutrients can cause coral tissue recession. Target ranges: NO3 5-10 ppm, PO4 0.02-0.05 ppm.

steps.title: Emergency Response Protocol
steps.description: For water quality emergencies, follow this response checklist:
checklistItems: Stop any ongoing additions or corrections
Assess coral condition (stress signs, polyp extension)
Determine if emergency water change is needed
Make gradual adjustments over hours, not minutes

steps.title: Water Change Procedures
steps.description: Routine water changes maintain stable chemistry and remove accumulated waste. Change 10-20% of system volume weekly or bi-weekly depending on bioload. New saltwater must be mixed at least 24 hours in advance and temperature/salinity matched to system. Test new water before adding. Add water slowly or use a drip system to prevent rapid parameter changes. Never exceed 25% water change in a single session without gradual acclimation.

steps.title: Record Keeping Requirements
steps.description: Maintain complete water quality records including:
checklistItems: Date, time, and tester for each measurement
All parameter readings (even if within range)
Reagent lot numbers and expiration dates
Salt mix brand and batch used
Coral health observations correlated with WQ data

steps.title: Trend Analysis and Reporting
steps.description: Review water quality data weekly to identify trends. Plot parameters over time to visualize stability or drift. Correlate water quality events with observed coral behavior or health changes. Monthly summary reports should include: parameter ranges, number of excursions, interventions performed, and equipment issues. Use trend analysis to predict and prevent future problems rather than just reacting to current conditions.
